criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Need is compelling and Australian-focused: GBR bleaching history, users (marine/conservation scientists, reef managers), and a plausible new capability (colour/tone detection applied to GBR). Literature is referenced. However no quantified requirements — resolution, revisit, spectral bands, coverage, lifetime — are stated, so objectives stay qualitative. Top-of-level is not warranted.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Dated Gantt chart with completed/planned coding, deadlines marked, and task-by-task explanation tying each stage to mission segments (launch, orbit, ground, comms, disposal). Iterative strategy pruning and a week-10 buffer show some contingency thinking, but no explicit fallback if launch, orbit or STK work fails. Information sources listed separately.

evidence.quote: This research will be ongoing throughout almost the entire design process as I will be learning and designing in parallel.
Week 10 is reserved for review, amendments, final simulations, and reflection.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is limited to reading plus four STK tutorials; no orbit, link-budget, coverage or payload results are presented, and no tutorial outputs or interpretations are shown. Desktop research is relevant but the technical evidence to date is minor, matching the adequate descriptor.

evidence.quote: researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and readable prose. But the Gantt figure lacks a number and caption, the source list repeats items already footnoted and duplicates themselves, and no listed source except the four footnotes is cited in text — in-text citations and reference list do not match.

technical_issues.issue: Ocean acidification is presented as causing bleaching; bleaching is driven primarily by thermal stress. Acidification is a separate stressor and the causal chain is wrong.
"30 percent more acidic" is a loose restatement of a ~30% rise in hydrogen-ion concentration (pH drop ~0.1); the wording overstates change in pH.
No instrument concept or measurable mission requirements (GSD, spectral bands, revisit, swath, data latency, lifetime) despite claiming finer bathymetry and near-real-time relay.
Footnote 4 is a Nature news item, not primary literature; the Asner sensor's applicability to satellite orbit is asserted without supporting performance data.
No contingency for key risks: launch vehicle/trajectory selection failing, STK licence or simulation problems, or schedule slip before the 20/11 deadline beyond a single review week.
Ground segment reasoning is speculative ("maybe only one is required"); no consideration of contact duration, data volume or downlink capacity.
Source list is unannotated and repeats footnoted items; the role of each source in the design is not indicated.

overall: Strong, well-written rationale for a GBR monitoring satellite with a workable dated Gantt plan. Weaknesses: no quantified mission requirements, negligible technical results beyond STK tutorials, and an inconsistent reference list. A solid foundation that needs specifications and real analysis.

feedback.summary: Your rationale for a Great Barrier Reef monitoring satellite is clear, Australian-focused and well written, and your dated Gantt plan is workable. To reach the top level, you need quantified mission requirements, corrected science statements, a fuller contingency plan, real preliminary results from your STK work, and a consistent reference list.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, state measurable requirements (ground sample distance, spectral bands, revisit, swath, data latency, lifetime). Correct the causal chain so bleaching is linked mainly to thermal stress, and restate the '30 percent more acidic' claim as a rise in hydrogen-ion concentration.

In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, add fallbacks for launch vehicle or trajectory selection, STK licence or simulation problems, and schedule slip before 20/11. Analyse the ground segment with contact duration, data volume and downlink capacity rather than 'maybe only one is required'.

Present your STK tutorial outputs (1 to 4) with brief interpretation of what they mean for your design. Number and caption Image 1 and any tables, and make every in-text citation match the reference list. Replace footnote 4 with primary literature, and annotate each source in Useful Links with its role in your design.

criteria.C1: You clearly identify the Great Barrier Reef context, its bleaching history, and users such as marine and conservation scientists and reef managers, linking each to a plausible new monitoring capability. To reach the top band, quantify your objectives with measurable requirements (resolution, spectral bands, revisit, swath, latency, lifetime). Correct the bleaching and acidification causal chain, restate the '30 percent' claim precisely, and replace the Nature news footnote with primary literature supporting the Asner sensor claim.
criteria.C2: Your dated Gantt chart and task-by-task explanation tie each stage to mission segments such as launch, orbit, ground, communications and disposal, and the week 10 review buffer shows some planning for contingency. To reach the top band, add explicit fallbacks for failure of launch, orbit or STK work and for schedule slip. Analyse the ground segment properly, and link each information source to the specific tasks it supports.
criteria.C3: You have completed desktop research on coral bleaching and four STK tutorials, which is relevant groundwork. The evidence of technical progress is currently minor, with no orbit, coverage, link-budget or payload results shown. To reach the next band, present a set of preliminary results from your STK work with brief interpretation, so the reader can see you are clearly on track for completion.
criteria.C4: Your report has clear headings and readable prose, which gives a good base. To reach the next band, number and caption all figures and tables, keep formatting consistent, and ensure every in-text citation matches the reference list. Remove the duplicated items in Useful Links and annotate each source to show how it informs your design.
